newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ROBSON CALM DESPITE REAL'S "WHITE CHRISTMAS" WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ROBSON CALM DESPITE REAL'S "WHITE CHRISTMAS" WIN.

text.p: Barcelona manager Bobby Robson was quick to reject suggestions the 2-0 defeat in Saturday's needle match against arch-rivals Real Madrid might prove decisive in this season's Spanish championship race.
"There are 78 points left, and we certainly shouldn't get nervous" said the former England manager, whose side slipped to third on Sunday after Deportivo Coruna's 1-0 victory over Valencia.
Deportivo's game with Barcelona has been postponed, along with all league fixtures scheduled for December 29th, until February, to give the players a longer Christmas break.
And with just one weekend of fixtures left this year, Barca will have to wait until at least January to clamber back to the top of the table.
"White Christmas," gloated Madrid sports daily As in the wake of Real's triumph, referring to the side's famous all-white team colours.

Critics stressed the contrast between the order of Real and the anarchy of Barcelona, and striker Barca's Ronaldo was targetted for failing to put away a rebound halfway through the second half when it appeared easier to score than miss.
"I had a lot of chances, but I missed them," said the young Brazilian. "But I'll take this thorn out, I will take revenge in the next game."

The match seemed to confirm that Ronaldo, who has scored over half his 13 league goals from individual runs launched from outside the penalty area, is not strong in the air and lacks a striker's killer instinct.
In contrast, Real's Croat Davor Suker drew level with Ronaldo in the Spanish goalscoring tables thanks to a characteristically opportunistic effort in the first half at the Bernabeu stadium.
Suker and the rest of the Real team were warmly praised by Saturday's other goalscorer, Predrag Mijatovic.
"I've got the best team mates in the world," said Mijatovic, who thanked Suker for his support during a week in which the Montenegrin's young son had to undergo an emergency operation.
But while the ecstatic Real players were praising themselves, others in Spain were criticising the exhaustive media coverage in the run-up to the match.

"They haven't done Spanish football much of a favour by talking for ten days about something that really doesn't mean anything," said Deportivo Coruna president Augusto Lendoiro. "It seems that Valencia, Atletico (Madrid) or ourselves don't signify anything."
Lendoiro's outspoken Atletico Madrid counterpart Jesus Gil weighed in by telling reporters how bad he thought the game had been.

Official statistics for Saturday's match have not been released, but it appears likely the clash will displace Spain's vital World Cup qualifier with Denmark in 1993 in the all-time television viewing figures.

The country's best-loved cartoonist Mingote pictured a man in an empty town square proclaiming "I love football and the calm with which I can walk through the city", and the ABC newspaper published a photo, taken on Saturday night, of Madrid's deserted streets which are normally heaving with revellers at the weekend.

Two fans with tickets for the match were forced to watch it on television after failing breathalyser tests at the turnstiles. Others struggled to find room to stand in the stadium because supporters were taking up precious space by sitting in standing areas.
